primary_claim: Frontier language models' ability to solve tasks without any chain-of-thought reasoning (no-CoT), measured by a 50%-success time horizon across 43 benchmarks, has doubled roughly every year since 2019, reaching about three minutes of human-equivalent task time for GPT-5.5; this no-CoT time horizon has grown roughly half as fast as METR's with-CoT time horizon since the release of GPT-4.

effect.value: 373 days [167, 691] 95% CI, R²=0.84, vs METR's with-CoT doubling time of 182 days, R²=0.92

contradicts_or_qualifies: Extends Ryan Greenblatt's prior no-CoT math time-horizon research to a broader 43-benchmark suite spanning math, coding, knowledge, agentic tool-use, and safety-relevant domains

Qualifies METR's with-CoT time-horizon doubling trend (182 days): shows the no-CoT time horizon grows roughly half as fast (373 days) since GPT-4, implying much of the post-GPT-4 increase in with-CoT capability comes from CoT itself rather than underlying no-CoT reasoning ability
stated_future_work: AI companies should start tracking no-CoT time horizons explicitly to find a lower bound on how much reasoning a model could do without revealing it to a CoT monitor or human
limitations_stated: uncertainty in the reasoning-token-anchor difficulty metric is not modeled, unlike human solve-time uncertainty which is calibrated with a noise model
questions that no evaluated no-CoT model solves but that o3-mini also fails to solve with reasoning are dropped from the reasoning-token-anchor analysis
quote: We find that frontier models like GPT-5.5 answer questions that take humans roughly three minutes with 50% reliability, and this TH has doubled approximately every year since 2019.
